chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the minimum energy needed to remove the outermost electron from an isolated gaseous atom; it generally decreases down a group and increases across a period. Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added to an isolated atom to form a uni-negative ion; it generally decreases down a group and increases across a period.
stem: Briefly describe ionization energy and electron affinity along with their trends in groups and periods.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
modelAnswer: Down a group, atomic size increases because an additional electron shell is added. Ionization energy decreases because shielding increases and the outer electron is easier to remove. Electronegativity generally decreases because the valence shell is farther from the nucleus and more shielded.
stem: How do atomic size, ionization energy and electronegativity vary down the group?

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
keyPoints: Alkaline earth metals: two valence electrons/+2
Ionization energy decreases down a group
modelAnswer: Alkali metals have one valence electron and form +1 ions; alkaline-earth metals have two valence electrons and generally require more energy to remove the first electron because their effective nuclear attraction is greater. In both families, ionization energy decreases down the group as shielding and atomic size increase.
stem: Briefly explain the difference in ionization energies of alkali and alkaline earth metals.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
keyPoints: Atomic size increases down Group IIA
Ionization energy decreases down Group IIA
modelAnswer: Down Group IIA, atomic size increases because additional electron shells are added. Ionization energy decreases because shielding increases and the outer electron is easier to remove. Electronegativity generally decreases because the valence shell is farther from the nucleus and more shielded.
stem: Periodic trends of Group IIA atomic size, ionization energy, electronegativity.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
modelAnswer: As Group IIA is descended, atomic size increases because a new shell is added. Ionization energy decreases because shielding weakens the nucleus–valence-electron attraction. Electronegativity also generally decreases as the valence electrons become farther from the nucleus.
stem: Predict the trend of atomic size, ionization energy and electronegativity of Group IIA using knowledge of chemical periodicity.
